frames.narration: The word 'lowest' arrives as text. The model cannot read letters, only integer IDs.
The tokenizer breaks it into the smallest pieces and adds a marker for the end of the word.

messages.label: l o w e s t _

frames.narration: It applies the merges in the order they were learned. 'l o w' becomes 'low', and 'e s t _' becomes 'est_'.

messages.label: merges: es, est, est_, lo, low

frames.narration: Only two tokens are left. A word the tokenizer has seen often costs very little.

A rarely seen word like 'xylophone' has few useful merges (only lo and ne apply), so it falls apart into 8 small tokens and costs more. Its letters x, y, p and h are not even in this toy vocabulary; a byte-level tokenizer would fall back to bytes for them.
Each token ID is looked up as a row in the embedding table, and the model works on those vectors from here on.
